If you only remember one thing: the A I race is starting to run into rules. Sam Altman is weighing a global watchdog. Washington banned Deep Seek in federal agencies. And Beijing drafted its own A I export controls.

Section one. The A I safety endgame. From your Rundown. Sam Altman reportedly told Open A I staff about three possible endings for the safety race. A global watchdog, like the International Atomic Energy Agency. A merger of the top labs, like CERN. Or one lab racing ahead, which he called terrible. He says Open A I must pick a path within a year. Why it matters: the biggest lab is openly talking about speed limits for self improving A I.

Section two. Money and models. Open A I will bring its models to Google's cloud, expanding beyond Microsoft. Bob McGrew, the former Open A I research chief, launched a startup called Arda at a one point five billion dollar valuation. It helps factories set up assembly lines faster. Chat G P T added new voices in six languages, with the A P I coming soon. And Perplexity's Computer can now rebuild apps without their source code. Anthropic and Open A I are also reportedly sketching wealth sharing plans ahead of I P Os. Why it matters: alliances are shifting, and copying a product is getting cheap.

Section three. Tech geopolitics. The Department of Homeland Security banned Deep Seek in federal civilian agencies, the same weekend Deep Seek shipped a faster model. And China released draft export controls on October sixteenth. They cover large A I models, agents, and big computing clusters. Fourteen technologies would be prohibited, twenty six would need a license. Public comment runs until November fifteenth. Your Recode China A I newsletter says publicly released open weight models look to be outside the scope. Why it matters: A I is now treated as strategic technology on both sides.

Section four. Media and comms. Your Comms Stack newsletter looks at what a dozen fall job interviews revealed about how companies see A I. Why it matters: it shows how employers talk about A I when hiring communications people.

Section five. Good news. The International Rescue Committee is urging the tech industry to put A I to work for the world's displaced people. Fortune also ran a piece on responsible A I in humanitarian aid. And from your Rundown, Claude is being applied to scorpion antivenom. Why it matters: A I work is starting to reach crisis response.

Also in your Reads. The New Yorker Daily covers Trump's golf course crusade, how I C E is targeting the midterms, and whether Wikipedia can survive.

The thread today: rules are catching up with the models, at home and abroad. Have a great day.
